title: BWP vs MR plywood: which to use where
excerpt: Both are good plywood, but they are built for different conditions. Here is how to pick the right one for each part of your home.
author: Comfort Nest Team

content.text: Walk into any plywood shop and the first question is usually BWP or MR. The choice affects cost and how long your furniture lasts, so it is worth understanding.

MR stands for moisture resistant. It is bonded with urea formaldehyde resin, which handles humidity and the occasional damp cloth but not sustained water. BWP stands for boiling waterproof. It uses phenolic resin, which holds up to prolonged moisture and even hot water in standard tests, and the Indian standards IS:303 (MR) and IS:710 (marine/BWP) describe these types.

items: Living-room units, shelves and TV cabinets
Drawers and internal partitions in dry rooms
Kitchen base units, especially around the sink and hob
Balcony and ground-floor rooms with damp walls
Any area where leaks or condensation are likely

content.text: BWP typically costs noticeably more per sheet. A practical approach is to spend it where water is a real threat and use MR elsewhere. Using BWP for the whole house rarely pays back, while using MR under a kitchen sink often leads to swollen panels.

items: Check the thickness: 18 mm is common for carcasses, 12 mm for backs and shelves of light use
Ask for the brand's grade marking and a bill with the brand name
Seal cut edges and use laminate or edge banding on all exposed faces
Match the grade to the worst conditions the piece will see, not the average

content.text: If you are unsure, tell us which room and which unit you are building and we will suggest a grade and thickness.
